geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from split wings into a courtyard macro so the ground response becomes legible and public.
Widen the court to create a meaningful open-space figure rather than a narrow gap.
Open the court toward the program access side so the street threshold is explicit.

graph_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant split-wing into a courtyard macro so the mass produces a real public void instead of a collision seam.
Open the center more aggressively so the void reads as inhabitable and usable.
Align the public opening with the verified access side to strengthen the street threshold.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent compact mass in multi-view and does not collapse into a single-view trick, but it is still primarily two rectangular bars with a narrow seam between them. That gives decent gesture clarity and repair integrity, yet the dominant spatial idea is underdeveloped for neighborhood_living because the ground response to the access edge is weak and the open-space figure is not legible as a usable court/terrace. The split-wing logic offers some precedent resonance, but the mass feels semantically closer to a generic interlocked office/pavilion arrangement than a neighborhood street building with an active threshold. Sectionally, there is little evidence of a calm upper hierarchy supporting a clear public ground condition, so program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and curved than the candidate; the candidate lacks the same legible courtyard/public opening.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and a bridging connector can produce a clear public threshold for neighborhood-scale programs.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Aerial campus condition is much larger and less directly analogous to this compact massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a shared open center can support mixed neighborhood uses when the void is the organizing figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is too blocked-up and does not establish the same open center or roof continuity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long low mass with a pronounced central atrium/void and a roof that reads as one continuous section can anchor neighborhood-scale program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate hints at splitting, but the void is too narrow and the overall continuity is weaker.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Spread-out wings with bridges and terraces can make a public courtyard and hierarchical section feel embedded in the mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate reads as two similar blocks colliding rather than a more resolved interlocking system.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking low-rise volumes with voids under elevated masses can maintain a clear main/support relationship while keeping ground public.

warnings: Visible access-edge response is too sealed/indeterminate for the required active street threshold.
The void between masses is too narrow and reads more like a collision seam than public space.
The form is coherent, but the program relation is not strong enough for neighborhood living.
